result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a two-lane residential street with continuous sidewalks, though they are obstructed by utility poles. The intersection lacks basic safety features like marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control devices, creating a high-risk environment for crossing.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection in the foreground lacks marked crosswalks, increasing risk for pedestrians crossing.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the sidewalk path, narrowing the effective walking width.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large white van parked near the intersection may block the view between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The street environment features continuous sidewalks but lacks basic pedestrian crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. Parked vehicles near the intersection and wide travel lanes create visibility issues and potential for higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No painted crosswalks are visible at the intersection, making pedestrian intent less clear to drivers.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the corner block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line near the intersection

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: A vehicle is parked partially on the sidewalk/apron area, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: In front of the vacant lot next to the grey building

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The street features a wide, straight roadway with two travel lanes and on-street parking, which may encourage higher vehicle speeds. While sidewalks are present on both sides, they lack buffers from traffic and there are no marked pedestrian crossings visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Wide roadway
hazards.description: The wide, straight asphalt surface without traffic calming measures likely encourages vehicle speeds above a safe urban limit.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both curbs block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street along the curb

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated and safer place for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Plant street trees to create a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, while also narrowing the perceived width of the street to slow traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a mid-block commercial environment with a continuous sidewalk and on-street parallel parking. While a dedicated walkway exists, it lacks a buffer from the roadway and is partially obstructed by a utility pole.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is positioned within the sidewalk's clear path, narrowing the walkable area.
hazards.location_in_image: Left-center, on the sidewalk in front of the brick building.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical or horizontal separation (like a planting strip or furniture zone) between the sidewalk and the parking/travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire length of the curb line.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clear Zone Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure a consistent clear path by relocating or consolidating utility infrastructure away from the primary walking zone.
